chunks: That [is the case], and whoever honors the sacred ordinances of God, it is better for him with his Lord. And the cattle are made lawful for you except what is recited to you, so avoid the impurity of the idols and avoid the saying of falsehood.
ai.seo_question: What are the sacred ordinances of God and what dietary restrictions are mentioned in this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Hajj is pivotal for establishing the hierarchy of divine commands, linking the internal virtue of honoring 'hurumat' (sacred boundaries) with external rituals like the Hajj and dietary laws. It serves as a comprehensive guide for believers, connecting the avoidance of idolatry (rijs) and false speech (qawl al-zur) to the purity of both action and creed, reinforcing the concept of 'tawhid' in practice.
